intro: Change audio speed speeds up or slows down a recording: listening to a lecture or a podcast in less time, slowing down a song to learn it on an instrument, going through a dictation calmly or adjusting the length of a voice-over. It accepts MP3, WAV, OGG, OPUS, M4A, AAC, FLAC, AIFF, WMA and AMR.

The speed ranges from 0.25 to 4: 1 leaves the audio unchanged, 1.5, the default, makes it 50 % faster, 2 makes it twice as fast and 0.5 plays it at half speed. The duration changes in the same proportion: a 60-minute lecture at 1.5 lasts 40.

With «Keep the pitch», on by default, voices do not sound high when sped up or low when slowed down: FFmpeg's atempo filter is used, chained several times when the speed goes above 2 or below 0.5. If you turn it off, the audio changes speed like a record or a tape, and the pitch goes up or down with it; sometimes that is exactly the effect you want.

The processing runs on our server. By default the result comes out in the same format as the original, except AMR, which comes out as MP3; under more options you can ask for MP3 or WAV. The file name carries the speed, for example «lecture-x1,5.mp3», and with several files you also get a ZIP.
steps: Upload one or more audio files.
Enter the speed and decide whether to keep the pitch.
Download the audio at its new speed.

faq.q: Can I use speeds like 1.25 or 0.8?
faq.a: Yes, any value between 0.25 and 4 with decimals: for example, 1.25 to listen to something a little faster or 0.8 to follow a song more easily.
It looks at the length of the audio you upload: up to 10 minutes without an account, 30 minutes with a free account and 4 hours on Pro. It does not matter that speeding it up makes it shorter.

faq.q: Can I change the pitch without changing the speed?
faq.a: No, this tool changes the speed. When you turn off «Keep the pitch», pitch and speed change together.
